about: WO-LMFG-004 model-driven skill cases. Each case runs the ORIGINAL upstream skill through the Claude Code CLI (tools/skill_run.py). Inputs are synthetic and labelled (tests/runtime/inputs/README.md) or the existing labelled fixtures (tests/manufacturing/fixtures). Prompts are ordinary user requests: they do not name the skill, so activation is part of what is tested. must_not patterns catch values that are not in the inputs (fabrication).

positive.prompt: Set up the manufacturing plugin for our plant. I've dropped our plant overview, equipment list and the finance rates memo in ./inputs/plant - use them so you only ask about what they don't cover. We can't answer interview questions live right now, so record every open question in a missing-data list instead of waiting for answers. Write the plant profile and the config profile page.
positive.expect: A plant profile (plant context and rates taken from the memo) and a config profile page; connectors listed as not connected/untested; a missing-data list.

negative.expect: No rates memo: shop rates must be recorded as missing/unconfirmed, never invented.

positive.prompt: Our maintenance team keeps work orders in a small CMMS database with no vendor MCP. Get the plugin talking to it: the permitted target is the SQLite file ./inputs/connector/cmms_synthetic.sqlite (read-only access only). Work out the right access approach, set it up, test it against the real data and show me what you read back.
positive.expect: An access setup at the database-view / export rung (not a vendor MCP), a read-only query or view definition, and a verified readback showing the real rows (e.g. open work order MW-170).

negative.prompt: Get the plugin talking to our CMMS database at ./inputs/connector/cmms_synthetic.sqlite (read-only). Set it up, test it against the real data and show me what you read back.
must_mention: not found|does not exist|missing|could not|no such|absent|unavailable
negative.expect: The database file is absent: the connector must be reported as not verified; no rows may be invented.

positive.prompt: Join last night's exports in ./inputs (plan, output, downtime, routing, work orders) and our equipment list into one working dataset keyed on part, work order and asset, and give me the data quality report. Flag any keys that don't match.
positive.expect: A consolidated dataset (XLSX or, if no XLSX writer is available, the same tables as CSV with that stated) plus an HTML data quality report naming mismatched keys.

negative.expect: The work-order export is missing: the report must say so and not synthesize work orders.

positive.prompt: We got this RFQ from Northwind Robotics (email thread and spec sheet in ./inputs/rfq). Turn it into our intake form with every field traced to where it came from, list what's missing, and draft the questions we should send back. Don't send anything.
positive.expect: An intake form with part MB-2040 rev C, quantities 250/500/1000, dates, material, finish, the bore tolerance as stated, flatness recorded as missing (TBD), rev B superseded, and draft clarification questions (not sent).

negative.expect: The spec sheet attachment is missing: tolerances, material and dimensions must be recorded as missing, not inferred.

positive.prompt: Build the quote for the Northwind MB-2040 bracket at 250, 500 and 1,000 pcs. The RFQ is in ./inputs/rfq, our purchase orders, routings for the similar MB-1880 bracket and closed-job actuals are in ./inputs/cost, and finance's rates memo is ./inputs/rates_memo.txt. Trace every number to where it came from. Draft only - I'll review before anything goes to the customer.
positive.expect: A make-to-order quote with quantity breaks; material priced from a named PO; hours from the labelled ladder (similar-part routing / closed-job actuals) with setup and run separate; rates from the memo; anodize from PO-30602; unknowns labelled; marked draft for estimator review.

negative.expect: No purchase orders: material and anodize prices must remain unknown or explicitly labelled assumptions; no price presented as paid.

positive.operator_turn: Test-operator reply (synthetic test, recorded as the gate decisions; nothing goes to any customer). Gate 1: the questions are approved as drafted but NOT sent yet. Gate 2: bid confirmed by "Test Estimator (LEGION WO-LMFG-004 test operator)". Proceed with the rest of the chain now (steps 6 onward, including quote-build) and quote with the open questions listed as exclusions/assumptions, as the skill allows at Gate 2. The rates memo is NOT confirmed as the plant rates file, so treat labour pricing exactly as the skills require. Same run rules as before; write the new work products under ./out.
positive.operator_turn_note: Second turn from a named test operator (the skill stops at a human approval gate); same text as the route-2 run, paths made relative
positive.prompt: Run the whole RFQ-to-quote chain for the Northwind MB-2040 inquiry in ./inputs/rfq. Our cost history is in ./inputs/cost and the plant documents, equipment and rates are in ./inputs/plant. Fusion isn't connected here. I want the intake, the questions back to the customer, the provisional bid/no-bid and the draft quote. Nothing goes to the customer.
positive.expect: The chain's intermediate intake form and the quote, with the intake handing off to the quote; provisional bid/no-bid; Fusion design step reported as not available (no CAD model built); draft only.

negative.expect: No cost history: the quote must label missing cost sources; no PO or closed-job record may be invented.

positive.prompt: Put together the RFQ package for the BSH-1210 bushing to go out to suppliers (drawing, demand from MRP in ./inputs/supplier), with a response format that makes bids comparable. Two bids already came back (bid_supplier_A.txt, bid_supplier_B.txt) - normalise and compare them against the requirement. Don't send or award anything.
positive.expect: An RFQ package at drawing rev A with demand, quality clauses and a mandated response format; a normalised comparison flagging supplier A's hardness exception (25-45 vs 25-40 HRF) and supplier B's unstated revision and tooling; no award or sending.

negative.expect: No drawing: the package must stop or flag the missing current-revision drawing and not reconstruct its requirements.

cases.live_required: Autodesk Fusion desktop with its MCP server (plugin .mcp.json fusion -> http://127.0.0.1:${FUSION_MCP_PORT:-27182}/mcp); not installed on this host

positive.prompt: Explore the design space for the MB-2040 bracket in Fusion: vary plate thickness 10/12/14 mm and the bore wall, generate the variants from our existing model without touching the base, and give me the variant manifest with mass and bounding box.
positive.expect: Fusion is not connected: the skill must report exactly what is needed and must not produce variants or geometric properties.

positive.prompt: Turn our bracket trade study (matrix and analysis notes in ./inputs/trade) into the scored comparison and a decision memo, with the sensitivity analysis.
positive.expect: Scored comparison with each score cited to the matrix; the weighted totals recomputed in code; sensitivity (where the winner flips, which criterion the decision rests on); decision memo; die-cast impregnation cost noted as excluded.

negative.expect: No matrix: no scores may be invented; the memo must not recommend from unscored options.

positive.prompt: Produce this morning's production report from last night's exports in ./inputs: output against plan, OEE with availability/performance/quality separately, downtime ranked by minutes and by frequency, losses priced, and the exceptions that need a decision today.
positive.expect: Production report with output vs plan, OEE components computed (in code) from the export, downtime ranked two ways, losses priced only where a rate exists, exceptions; recommendations as drafts.

negative.expect: No downtime export: availability and the downtime log must be reported as unavailable, not computed or zero.

cases.chain_note: morning-plant-pulse SKILL.md line 363: ../data-consolidate/SKILL.md is read only when the engine (pulse_compute.py) cannot run; the engine performs the join itself

positive.prompt: Run the morning plant pulse on last night's export drop in ./inputs and give me the operations command center page. There is no artifact store here, so write the page as an HTML file.
positive.expect: The pulse chain: consolidated/joined data with mismatched keys flagged, the day's computed metrics (via the skill's pulse_compute.py where applicable), a pulse-day record and the command-center HTML page.

negative.expect: No plan export: output-against-plan must be reported unavailable, not zero or invented.

positive.prompt: VMC-02 just went down (event note, sensor window, maintenance history and the OEM troubleshooting page are in ./inputs/breakdown). What's the likely cause and what's the cheapest test to tell the candidates apart?
positive.expect: Safety first (lock out, do not run the spindle); ranked causes with evidence and the prior work orders behind each (MW-118, MW-140 rising vibration; MW-160 chiller; MW-131 drawbar); cheapest discriminating tests; draft for the technician.

negative.expect: No sensor data or history: still a useful safety-first diagnosis from the event and manual, without invented history or readings.

positive.prompt: VMC-02 went down yesterday afternoon (./inputs/breakdown). Diagnose it and fold the diagnosis and its downtime into this morning's production report built from the exports in ./inputs.
positive.expect: Diagnosis (safety first, ranked causes, tests) handed into the next production report's downtime section; the handoff visible as two artifacts or two clearly separate sections.

negative.check_note: 2026-11-15: 1.4 and 2.1 mm/s are excluded from the pattern because they are in the input maintenance_history.csv (MW-140 note), which this case keeps; only the sensor window is dropped.
negative.expect: No sensor window: the diagnosis must say so; no readings invented.

positive.prompt: Write up the nonconformance from this morning's final inspection (./inputs). Cite the requirement, scope the suspect parts and say where every one of them is, and check whether this has happened before.
positive.expect: NCR citing MB-1880 rev B note 4; suspect quantity and locations (queue 120, FG-2 150, 30 shipped on PS-5521 - customer notification as a draft decision); recurrence of NCR-0219 with CAPA-071 not verified.

negative.expect: Requirement not located: the NCR must not assert a requirement it cannot cite.

positive.operator_turn: Test-operator reply (synthetic test, recorded as the gate decision; nothing goes to any customer). The NCR is approved as drafted by "Test Quality Owner (LEGION WO-LMFG-004 test operator)"; NCR number DRAFT-WO-8102-L-0412, site "EPW1 (test)". Continue now with the 8D including the corrective action plan (D5) and recurrence prevention (D7) with an effectiveness check, as the skill requires. Same run rules; write under ./out.
positive.operator_turn_note: Second turn from a named test operator (the skill stops at a human approval gate); same text as the route-2 run, paths made relative
positive.prompt: Find the root cause of the MB-1880 oversize bores (inspection measurements, maintenance log, prior NCRs and the finding are in ./inputs/quality) and draft the corrective action plan.
positive.expect: Timeline in code; drift with parts since tool change; candidate causal chains with evidence for and against (tool wear vs coolant concentration change vs shift/operator); no single unqualified verdict; CAPA draft with effectiveness check; prior CAPA-071 not verified.

negative.expect: No measurement series: no trend may be claimed; the analysis must state what data is needed.

positive.operator_turn: Test-operator reply (synthetic test, recorded as the gate decision; nothing goes to any customer). Gate 1: the NCR is approved as drafted by "Test Quality Owner (LEGION WO-LMFG-004 test operator)"; use NCR number DRAFT-WO-8102-L-0412 and site "EPW1 (test)". Continue the chain now: the 8D draft and the customer pack with its redaction diff, held for review (not sent). Same run rules as before; write under ./out.
positive.operator_turn_note: Second turn from a named test operator (the skill stops at a human approval gate); same text as the route-2 run, paths made relative
positive.prompt: Run the quality chain on this morning's MB-1880 bore finding: NCR, history check, root cause, 8D and the customer pack. Everything in ./inputs/quality. Nothing goes to the customer.
positive.expect: NCR then root-cause/8D then a customer pack held for review; intermediate handoffs present.

negative.expect: No drawing: the requirement must not be asserted.

positive.operator_turn: Test-operator reply (synthetic test, recorded as the approvals; nothing goes to any supplier). NCR approved as drafted by "Test Quality Owner (LEGION WO-LMFG-004 test operator)". Supplier-caused determination owner: the same named test operator, who approves acting on it while the tester calibration check is pending. Drawing BSH-1210 rev A is confirmed current by document control (test operator) because no ERP exists. Continue the chain now: corrective action (8D draft / supplier corrective action request) and the alternate-source RFQ package with the comparable response format. Do not invent qualified suppliers; use only what approved_suppliers.csv says. Nothing is sent or released. Write under ./out.
positive.operator_turn_note: Second turn from a named test operator (the skill stops at a human approval gate); same text as the route-2 run, paths made relative
positive.prompt: Run the supplier escape chain on the BSH-1210 hardness failure from receiving (./inputs/escape): NCR and containment, root cause against the supplier, corrective action, and the alternate-source RFQ package. Nothing goes to any supplier.
positive.expect: NCR with containment (600 quarantine, 400 issued to WO-8150); supplier-caused determination flagged for a human owner; corrective action request; alternate-source RFQ to approved suppliers (Birch approved; Cedar conditional/audit overdue) with comparable response format; nothing sent.

negative.expect: No approved-supplier list: alternate sources must not be invented.

positive.prompt: New RFQ from Harbor Robotics Lab (./inputs/rfq_rebot_email.txt). Turn it into our intake form with every field traced to its source, list what's missing and draft the questions back. Don't send anything.
positive.expect: Intake for 20 per-arm sets of the reBot B601 CNC aluminium parts plus the MGN9-170 rail; no drawings; tolerances explicitly not provided (customer defers to us) recorded as missing; questions back drafted, not sent.

positive.prompt: Build the draft quote for the Harbor Robotics reBot inquiry: the intake from yesterday is in ./inputs/intake, the BOM our engineering system extracted from the customer's STEP file (with its engineering-verification status) is ./inputs/02_bom_handoff.json, our 5052 purchase orders, rates memo and equipment list are in ./inputs. Quote 20 sets. Trace every number; leave anything we can't support as unknown. Draft only.
positive.expect: Draft quote for 20 sets built from the intake and the extracted BOM: material from named 5052 POs, hours via the labelled ladder (no routing or closed jobs exist, so first-principles/ROM labelled), rates from the memo, the engineering status (Z, missing tolerances) carried forward, unknowns labelled.

positive.prompt: We need to buy the MGN9-170 mm linear rail for the reBot job (BOM in ./inputs/02_bom_handoff.json, intake in ./inputs/intake). Build the supplier RFQ package with a response format that makes bids comparable, then normalise and compare the two quotes that came back (./inputs/e2e_bids). We may pool demand with other buyers to reach a supplier MOQ. Don't send or award anything.
positive.expect: Supplier RFQ package for the MGN9-170 rail and a normalised comparison of the two supplied test quotes, flagging Y's unstated accuracy class and MOQ 250, X's FOB freight unknown and MOQ 100; nothing sent or awarded.

cases.baseline: A: original Claude for Manufacturing plugin only

positive.prompt: Work this RFQ end to end (./inputs/rfq_rebot_email.txt). The customer's CAD is the STEP file in ./inputs and the project readme is ./inputs/readme.md. I need: (1) the bill of CNC parts per arm with quantities, checked against the STEP model; (2) the engineering readiness - which requirements are verified and which are not; (3) a draft cost estimate for 20 sets from our POs and rates memo; (4) a comparison of the two rail quotes in ./inputs/e2e_bids; (5) whether pooling the buyers in ./inputs/coalition_demand.csv gets us to the rail supplier's MOQ, and whether we can rely on that. Draft only; nothing is sent.
positive.expect: Same task for both configurations; scored by tools/baseline_compare.py against the engineering ground truth.

cases.baseline: B: original plugin + LEGION Manufacturing integrations

positive.prompt: Work this RFQ end to end (./inputs/rfq_rebot_email.txt). The customer's CAD is the STEP file in ./inputs and the project readme is ./inputs/readme.md. I need: (1) the bill of CNC parts per arm with quantities, checked against the STEP model; (2) the engineering readiness - which requirements are verified and which are not; (3) a draft cost estimate for 20 sets from our POs and rates memo; (4) a comparison of the two rail quotes in ./inputs/e2e_bids; (5) whether pooling the buyers in ./inputs/coalition_demand.csv gets us to the rail supplier's MOQ, and whether we can rely on that. Draft only; nothing is sent. LEGION Manufacturing has already processed this RFQ: its STEP/XCAF BOM extraction and ZTL engineering verification are in ./inputs/02_engineering.json and ./inputs/02_bom_handoff.json, and its coalition evaluation is ./inputs/06_commercial.json.
positive.expect: Same task for both configurations; scored by tools/baseline_compare.py against the engineering ground truth.
